items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: One is a Benge coronet that he, Eldon Alvin Benge made for me. ... He heard me play at a place called the 'Brass Rail' in Chicago

ctx.x: One is a Benge coronet that he, Eldon Alvin Benge made for me. He was the first trumpet player in the Chicago Symphony Orchestra for quite a few years. And he started, was making trumpets. But he heard me play at a place called the 'Brass Rail' in Chicago when I had Peewee Russell and George Brunis, Joe Sullivan, Eddie Condon and Dave Tough on drums. A good band. And Eldon Alvin Benge who was a marvellous musician, first trumpet player with the Chicago Symphony.

items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Alvin came in one night... he said, Jimmy, he said, give me your old horn... Wasn't that sweet of him? A wonderful man.

ctx.x: Now is that the one that you're blowing, that's the one you're blowing now?
